full_judgment: 11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner and also for respondent No. 2 and respondent Nos. 4 and 5 and also Dhaka Municipal Corporation and we find that in the instant case the dispute is over the creation of new sub-plots by means of a revised plan adding to the master plan and leasing it out to new allottees by the appropriate authority, namely Housing and Settlement Department from whom the petitioner AKM Faruque is also one of the lease holders being plot No. 5 of Section 2, Mirpur Housing Estate, which is adjacent to the newly created sub-plots No. 5(1) and 5(2). We have examined the master plan of the Mirpur Housing Estate which is annexed to the main writ petition by the petitioner being Annexure-'B'. From a reading of the said master plan it is seen that the said plan clearly mentioned where it is required to mention such as Road, Market, police station, wide road Graveyard, Lake, Playground etc. The vacant space in between Blocks E and F is not earmarked to be any road or market land or police station or mosque but just vacant and in front of which long vacant space at both ends there is a road marked as road in the master plan and in between the other blocks the crossing roads are numbered as Road No. 4, 5 and 6, 1,2,3, and Road No.8. This vacant space kept by the original framer of the plan in 1967 had not been marked for any particular purpose. The vacant land vested in the government within the residential zone are to be utilised for residential purposes by the government or for other amenities thereto. It appears that thereafter new plots were created terming them as rehabilitation plots in the said zone as or housing Estate within the master plan adding to the master plan. The new plots have been created on the same line one after the other, in a chain on the vacant side in between block E and F being new plot No. A(1), A(2), A(3), A(4), A(5) and in the chain thereafter, a new plot was created as "Police Station" and below that another two plots were created being plot Nos. 5(1) and 5(2) by keeping road No. 6 in front of plot No.1, 5, 5(1) and 5(2) as in the original plan, It is further seen from the revised plan Annexure-2 to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the Government at page 21 that in spite of the creation of plot Nos. 5 (1) and 5(2) on the part of eastern vacant side there is still 13 feet vacant space left after new plot on 5(1) and 5(2), from the other block. The petitioner can, so it appears, yet enter his plot from two ways namely Road No. 6 on the north and road No.8 on the south but vacant space of 13 ft. on the east would now be available to plot Nos. 5(1) and 5(2) because plot No. 5 shall have common boundary with Nos. 5(1) and 5(2) on the western side. This new site plan, clearly described to be a revised site plan and plots marked as rehabilitation plot. Those are created on the old vacant area starting from Mirpur Avenue No.1 ending in road No. 2 which covers in between a large number of other plots on the eastern side coming to main A venue and those plots are all in the vacant space in between. It is further seen that after creating the new plot A(l), A (2) and A(3) on the eastern north, facing the Avenue side, there is yet a vacant space of 40 ft at that end but at the bottom only 13 ft vacant space. We have examined the letter issued from the office of the Chief Engineer Housing and Settlement Estate and the letter for approval has been marked as an Annexure, which question of approval and non- approval has not been challenged in the original writ petition though it has been attempted to be agitated at the time of hearing of the petition and as that would be a question of fact not originally agitated in the petition we are not inclined to go into those facts and also for the reason that a plan once made is always capable of being revised thereafter by the marker and there is no bar to any revision or alteration and in the instant case the lease agreement with the new allottees having already been executed by the Directorate of Housing and Settlement and the established fact having been that the new allottees already with sanctioned plan from RAJUK had constructed their building in those newly leased out plots and the completion of the said construction by respondent Nos. 4 and 5 having been certified after local inspection, which is also in the affidavit-in-opposition of respondent Nos. 4 and 5 and when we have no reasons to doubt such a certificate given by an officer, in course of his official duty when presumption of its correctness under the Evidence Act would be evident, the question of sanction would not be relevant.
